newsitem.title: UK: TV reporter Bell delays UK anti-sleaze nomination.
newsitem.headline: TV reporter Bell delays UK anti-sleaze nomination.

text.p: Veteran war correspondent Martin Bell on Tuesday delayed handing in his nomination as an "anti-sleaze" candidate to stand against former Conservative minister Neil Hamilton, embroiled in a "cash-for-questions" row.
Bell wanted to stand as an "independent anti-corruption" candidate in the Tatton constituency in the May 1 election.
"When he went to submit the nomination this morning, he was advised by the returning officer that he may face a legal challenge," Bell's press spokeswoman, Kate Edgley, told Reuters.
"We are now consulting lawyers and wil return tomorrow to resubmit the nomination. This doesn't mean Hamilton is off the hook," she said.
Hamilton has denied allegations that he accepted money from a businessman in exchange for asking parliamentary questions and has steadfastly refused to stand down.
